calls.reason: The only evidence is one realized benefit, the MASAI trial's 44% cut in screen-reading workload. There is no inventory of claimed benefits, so 'almost every' can't be judged either way.

Official records show all three harms before publication: the FCC fine over the Biden deepfake robocalls, FBI reports of ongoing explicit deepfakes, and Senate testimony on an AI voice-clone kidnapping scam.
GPT-6 was released, but 'isn't magic' has no test, there is no deadline, and no matched measurement shows harm rising by many orders of magnitude.

Epoch shows training power doubling yearly, which supports the energy link. But Epoch also credits 5–40% of gains to algorithms, which cuts against the hedged 'only trick' half, so the evidence is mixed.
Stanford's genAI figure ($25.2B, over a quarter of AI investment) and PwC's $5B for AI climate start-ups don't split funding cleanly by type, and the emissions study is per task, not total harm.
